extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, research administrators, small business applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update page summarizing recent NIH policy, process, and resource changes relevant to NIH extramural grant applicants, awardees, and research administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of research models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose models based on appropriateness for the specific research question; while NIH encourages NAMs and human-relevant approaches, selection should be scientifically justified to maximize translational potential and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and potential splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should follow the specified application format, review the overview video for key features, and be aware that applications may be administratively split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan template/format when preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions; the format reflects a simplified set of required elements that applicants must include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations (Gold Standard Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate considerations of replication and reproducibility into study design, data practices, and application narratives where relevant; NIH is prioritizing and incentivizing replication/reproducibility across funding activities and highlighted topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the "Competitive But Not Discussed" (CBND) score designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Last November, NIH implemented emergency modifications to review processes following resumption of activities after the lapse in appropriations. Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving CBND should recognize it denotes the middle third of applications under the modified review process — competitive in score/rank but not discussed in full study section discussion; applicants should consult NIH guidance on implications for resubmission, Just-in-Time, and funding likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review objectives and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "One Year Later: How Centralized NIH Peer Review is Strengthening Efficiency, Competition, and Transparency" (consolidation of peer review within the Center for Scientific Review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The centralization of peer review is intended to affect review workflows, efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants should be aware that review processes and policies may change as a result and consult CSR guidance for impacts on submission and review expectations.
